review_notes: Independently reviewed the current 83-line proposal.json, the complete 45-line functionality.md, all 516 lines of fact-dispositions.json, and all 423 lines of link-dispositions.json. The current proposal differs from the prior librarian packet: it contains three purpose corrections, for OnReflect, ItemNessBatRemove, and ItemNessBatSetNULL. This verdict applies to the current proposal SHA only.

All three proposed writes are owned, supported, and appropriately bounded. OnReflect contains a fixed sound call, not a visual-effect operation. ItemNessBatRemove requests item removal before clearing the fighter slot. ItemNessBatSetNULL performs pointer bookkeeping without establishing completed item destruction. No replacement proposal is returned.

Read both owned files completely in canonical and rendered form, all four subject pages, and both link pages. The nine parameter subjects have no baseline facts. No compiled section or register-layout claim is accepted from source alone.

Verified the move mapping against the active Ness motion table and the common AttackS4 fighter dispatcher, rather than numeric motion names. Independently read the Ness-bat constructor, item state table, pickup selector, animation consumer, reciprocal owner clearing, and removal helper.

Verified the delegated physics branches, reflector flag clear and creator, animation-completion scan, conditional common completion dispatcher, Wait input selection, collision position synchronization, conditional Fall call, and Ness damage-handler call path.

Boundary review confirms zero versus nonzero command and interrupt gates, nullable creation and cleanup, reflector synchronization before the separate completion test, and cleanup before input-transition acceptance. Ground-speed equality does not select scaled friction. Signed-zero, NaN, and infinity comparison observations in functionality.md agree with the displayed source under ordinary floating comparison semantics; engine-wide nonfinite safety is not established.

The current ledgers correctly supersede the three purposes changed by the proposal and defer section contents, reflector timing, and unconditional damage-destruction assurance. Additional independently deferred details below do not require new writes: they are unsupported extensions of otherwise supported baseline descriptions.

All 20 existing implements relationships are supported. Historical locators and digests are preserved as baseline metadata, not substituted for current canonical evidence. Retaining a relationship does not validate an exact reflector interval or a general callback-lifetime guarantee.
